final_message:
The root cause was in `due_for_retry` in `billing/dunning.py`, and I've fixed it. The 24 tests pass, but I didn't add a test that reproduces the 8-attempts-instead-of-4 symptom.

The filter was `status == "open" or (next_attempt_at <= now)`. Because of the `or`, every open invoice counted as due on every cycle run, so the policy's `next_attempt_at` schedule was ignored. Invoices that had used up all their retries, and so had no next attempt, were also charged again.

An open invoice is now due in only two cases:
- It has a `next_attempt_at` that has arrived.
- It has never been attempted (`attempt_count == 0`).

I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}`.

steps.command:
python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''if invoice["status"] == "open" or invoice["next_attempt_at"] is not None and invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now''','''if invoice["status"] == "open"
        and (
            invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now
            if invoice["next_attempt_at"] is not None
            else invoice["attempt_count"] == 0
        )''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8
